title: Energon: Unveiling Transformers from GPU Power and Thermal Side-Channels
evidence_span: The paper investigates GPU power and thermal fluctuations as side channels for extracting transformer architectural details. It evaluates public language and vision transformers, reports over 89% average model-family identification accuracy and 100% hyperparameter classification in the abstract, and demonstrates transfer attacks with average success above 93%; the paper also describes a user-privilege threat model and responsible disclosure to NVIDIA.
problem: Shared or virtualized GPUs expose power and thermal telemetry that may leak proprietary transformer architecture information without physical access.
method_or_artifact: CNN-based predictors over power and thermal traces to infer transformer family, layer, and attention-head information, followed by substitute-model construction and black-box transfer attacks.
workload_or_benchmark: Eight publicly available language/vision model families, custom transformers, NVIDIA A40 data-center GPU inference, single-process and noisy multi-process settings.
metrics: over 93% average transfer-attack success in abstract
BERT score above 93 for substitute-model evaluation
limits: The evidence is an author preprint and the repository does not yet extract every table or repeat the experiments; telemetry access, GPU generation, co-tenancy assumptions, and mitigation effectiveness constrain generalization.

title: HLSDebugger: Identification and Correction of Logic Bugs in HLS Code with LLM Solutions
evidence_span: HLSDebugger addresses HLS logic debugging with a released labeled dataset of about 300K samples and an encoder-decoder model that jointly predicts bug location, bug type, and correction; the abstract reports performance above advanced LLMs such as GPT-4 for bug identification and more than 3X for bug correction.
problem: HLS logic debugging is labor-intensive, circuit data is scarce, logic bugs are harder than syntax bugs, and reliable test cases are often unavailable.
method_or_artifact: Open labeled HLS bug dataset and customized encoder-decoder LLM that performs multi-task bug-location identification, bug-type prediction, and code correction, optionally using HLS-tool information.
workload_or_benchmark: HLS code containing known logic-bug categories, without assuming additional test cases.
metrics: bug-identification performance above GPT-4 in reported evaluation
more than 3X bug-correction performance improvement over advanced LLMs
limits: The evidence is an author preprint; evaluation depends on the generated bug dataset and selected bug categories, and the repository has not yet extracted all accuracy, correction-validity, and generalization tables.

title: RSizing: Robust Bayesian Optimization for Analog Circuit Sizing Under Process Variations
evidence_span: RSizing uses a three-phase strategy: nominal-condition optimization to prune promising regions, heteroscedastic Gaussian processes to model non-uniform process-variation effects, and Thompson-sampling acquisition followed by targeted Monte Carlo refinement and calibration. Experiments on three benchmark circuits report robust designs that meet yield requirements while optimizing multiple performance metrics with lower computational cost.
problem: Analog circuit sizing under process variation is expensive and manual; nominal optimization can produce designs with poor yield when performance distributions shift across manufacturing variation.
method_or_artifact: Three-phase robust Bayesian optimization using nominal-region pruning, heteroscedastic Gaussian-process surrogate models, Thompson sampling, targeted Monte Carlo simulations, and model calibration.
workload_or_benchmark: Three analog benchmark circuits evaluated under process variation with multi-objective performance and yield requirements.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: CMOS analog circuit sizing and Monte Carlo process-variation simulation; exact technology node, circuit identities, and simulation budgets require full-paper extraction.
baselines: existing analog circuit sizing and Bayesian-optimization methods
limits: The evidence is an author-hosted conference PDF; the repository has not yet extracted numerical table values, exact baselines, technology assumptions, or all yield/quality tradeoffs.

title: VERIRL: Boosting the LLM-based Verilog Code Generation via Reinforcement Learning
evidence_span: VERIRL introduces Veribench-53K, curated from more than 700K Verilog problems with structured prompts, complexity labels, and testbenches. Its reinforcement-learning pipeline uses Trace-back based Rescore to improve sparse/noisy reward feedback and sample-balanced weighting to limit forgetting and overfitting; the abstract reports gains in test pass rate, functional correctness, and compilation robustness and releases the system publicly.
problem: Verilog generation is difficult for language models because of concurrency semantics, rigid syntax, simulation complexity, and sparse or noisy correctness feedback.
method_or_artifact: Reinforcement-learning framework for Verilog generation with a 53K-example dataset, Trace-back based Rescore, adaptive sample-balanced weighting, and co-evolving policy/reward models.
workload_or_benchmark: Verilog code-generation tasks with diverse testbenches and complexity labels, curated from more than 700K source problems.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: LLM-based HDL generation evaluated through compilation, simulation, and functional tests; exact model sizes, hardware, and test-suite composition require full-paper verification.
metrics: 53K curated training/evaluation examples from more than 700K problems
limits: The evidence is an author preprint and public repository; the repository has not independently reproduced the reported gains or verified benchmark splits, leakage controls, reward validity, and hardware cost.

title: Tasa: Thermal-aware 3D-Stacked Architecture Design with Bandwidth Sharing for LLM Inference
evidence_span: Tasa addresses the thermal limits of 3D-stacked architectures by combining heterogeneous high-performance and high-efficiency cores with cross-stack thermal optimization and bandwidth-sharing scheduling. The abstract reports peak-temperature reductions of 5.55, 9.37, and 7.91 degrees Celsius for 48, 60, and 72 core configurations, plus 2.85x and 2.21x speedups for Llama-65B and GPT-3 66B inference over GPU baselines and a heterogeneous PIM accelerator.
problem: 3D stacking increases memory bandwidth for autoregressive LLM decoding but creates more severe temperature, thermal-gradient, and scalability constraints than 2D designs.
method_or_artifact: Heterogeneous 3D-stacked architecture with high-performance cores for compute-intensive operators, high-efficiency cores for memory-intensive attention operators, cross-stack thermal balancing, and bandwidth-sharing scheduling.
workload_or_benchmark: Llama-65B and GPT-3 66B inference with 48-, 60-, and 72-core configurations; comparisons include GPU and heterogeneous PIM-based accelerators.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 3D-stacked multi-DRAM-die-over-logic architecture with thermal constraints and heterogeneous cores; technology, cooling, and memory-stack assumptions require full-paper verification.
limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; full-paper verification is needed for thermal-model calibration, area/cost overhead, memory bandwidth assumptions, and comparison fairness.
